prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Ideal Desktop Companion", "Select a starter friend or prepare photos for a custom companion tailored to your workspace."]
1: ["Preview Your Companion", "Check your companion look and traits before finalizing adoption.", "Looks Great!"]
2: []
3: ["Preparing Desktop Canvas", "Ensuring your companion has a safe screen position to spawn."]
4: ["You can add custom pets or change companion modes anytime later in app settings."]
5: ["Your pet is active on your desktop!", "Use the system tray icon to hide, summon, or talk with your pet anytime."]
6: ["For best results, upload well-lit front-facing photos with clear background contrast."]
7: ["Signing in automatically syncs your adoption progress and custom companion data to your account."]
8: ["Your companion is hatching in the background. We will alert you the moment it spawns!"]
9: ["Welcome to Your New Workspace Buddy!", "Your companion is ready on your screen. Double-click your pet to start your first chat!", "Start Exploring"]
